items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN! We built Meridian because we kept seeing the same thing: developers get estimates for planned work, and then spend a huge chunk of their time doing everything that wasn't planned.
Debugging something weird, helping a teammate, reviewing PRs, jumping on an incident, fixing a flaky test, answering questions, etc. All useful work, but a lot of it never makes it back into the estimate.

items.title: Show HN: Warp – Run the 313B GLM-5.3-Flash on a MacBook with 8GB RAM
items.contentSnippet:
A few months ago, I created the WARP engine (formerly WASTE) to run Kimi K3, the complete 2.78-trillion-parameter model, on macOS.
GLM-5.3-Flash shares many architectural similarities with Kimi K3, so I added support for it as well. It requires as little as 5.14 GB of RAM to run, and on a 64 GB MacBook Pro M5 Pro it reaches about 3.32 tok/s, or 3.86 tok/s on longer runs.
More memory means a larger expert cache, while higher storage and memory bandwidth can further improve performance.
